hints: A subarray sum is divisible by n exactly when its two prefix sums have the same remainder modulo n.
Count each remainder's earlier occurrences; each matching pair of prefix boundaries makes one valid subarray.
analogy: Prefix sums with the same remainder are separated by a whole multiple of n.
example: With n=5 and values 3,1,2,7,4, equal prefix remainders identify the valid segment [3,1,2,7].
algorithm: Start frequency[0]=1; accumulate prefix remainder ((sum%n)+n)%n, add its prior frequency to answer, then increment it.
correctness: Equal remainders imply their difference is divisible by n; every divisible-sum subarray has equal endpoint remainders.
complexity: O(n) time and O(n) frequency space.
